samples_judged.question_text: The pencils are placed in a row. One pencil is number 15 in the row. Which word describes its position?
Who arrived earlier: the student in 1st place or 19th place?
Write the symbol for the nineteenth position.
The pupils stand in a row. Jose is number 20 in the row. Which word describes Jose's position?
A runner is at position number 10. In what place did the runner finish?
The pupils stand in a row. Carlo is number 3 in the row. Which word describes Carlo's position?

verdicts.reasoning: Every stem but seed 23's is a request to say where something stands. Seeds 11, 64 and 103 hand the pupil a place in a line (pencil number 15, Jose at 20, Carlo at 3) and ask which word describes it; seeds 42, 91 and 127 invert that and ask for the word matching a given position; seed 57 asks for the written symbol of a spoken position. Seed 78's race finish is the same act in context. Seed 23 is a comparison of two positions rather than a description of one.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Stems that asked how many items are in the row, rather than where one of them stands, would not describe position.

verdicts.reasoning: Seed 11 is the lone sample with a non-human referent - pencils placed in a row - and it is the same pencil frame used at Grade 1. The other nine seeds either position people (students in seed 23, Jose and Carlo in seeds 64 and 103, a runner in seed 78) or supply no referent whatsoever (seeds 42, 57, 91, 118, 127 name only a bare position). The clause is met, but by a single seed and a single object noun.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Object contexts beyond pencils - books, chairs, beads on a string - appearing as keys in more than one seed would make this more than a one-sample showing.

verdicts.reasoning: All ten keys are ordinals. Symbol keys run 15th, 1st, 19th, 20th, 10th, 3rd and 4th (seeds 11, 23, 57, 64, 78, 103, 118); word keys are ninth, sixth and first (seeds 42, 91, 127). verdicts.reasoning: The band's upper end is answered, not just displayed. Seed 64 puts Jose at "number 20 in the row" and keys 20th; seed 57 keys 19th for the spoken "nineteenth", and seed 23 keys 1st in a stem that also prints 19th. Between those poles the samples land on 15th, 10th, ninth, sixth, 4th, 3rd and first (seeds 11, 78, 42, 91, 118, 103, 127), so the run from 1 to 20 is populated rather than clustered. The twentieth that appears in seed 91's options is redundant to the verdict.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Had 20th and 19th surfaced only among the distractors of seeds 91 and 118, the stated ceiling would be untested.
